note: Placement companies (P3MI) need a business licence (Art. 51, now under Law 6/2023, Art. 89A) and a Rp1.5 billion deposit (Art. 54(1)(b)), must resolve the problems of the workers they place (Art. 52(1)(c)) and stay responsible after revocation (Art. 58). source: Law 18/2017 Arts. 13, 15; KP2MI Regulation 3/2026 Art. 12 · official text: https://jdih.bp2mi.go.id/index.php/Content/produk/8/889000772

note: Minimum age 18 (Art. 5(a)). note: Recruitment agencies are licensed by the Department of Migrant Workers and are jointly and severally liable with the employer for claims; corporate officers are personally liable.
source: RA 8042 s. 10 as amended by RA 10022 s. 7; RA 11641 s. 3(h) · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/18116

source: RA 10801 ss. 4, 6(b), 8, 35; RA 8042 s. 37-A (RA 10022 s. 23) · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/67104

source: RA 11641 s. 15; RA 11299 · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/94035

source: RA 8042 s. 10 as amended; RA 11641 ss. 8(j), 9(c) · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/18116

note: The minimum age for household service workers is 23 for all genders (POEA GBR 2 s. 2007, lowering the 25 set in 2006; exemptions under GBR 4 s. 2011). Deployment to destinations can be restricted or banned (RA 8042 ss. 4–5; RA 11641 s. 8(k)); for Kuwait, deployment of first-time domestic workers has been deferred since 2023, and from 2024 only domestic workers with prior overseas experience may go (official guidance).

note: The National Reintegration Center for OFWs provides reintegration services and is now part of the DMW.
source: RA 8042 ss. 17–18 as amended by RA 10022 ss. 10–11; RA 11641 ss. 17, 19(e) · official text: https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/18116

note: Service enterprises need a licence, charter capital of VND 5 billion and a deposit (Arts. 7(5), 10, 24); they compensate only damage they cause (Art. 26(2)(h)); the Law sets no joint liability with the employer. Law 22/2026 (from 1 March 2027) moves licence procedures to a decree.
source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 7, 10, 24, 26 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

note: Service fees are capped at one month's salary per 12 months, three months at most (Art. 23(4)(a)), and may be collected only after the supply contract is approved and the placement contract signed (Art. 23(2)(c)); brokerage may not be charged to workers (Art. 7(8)). source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 7(8), 23; Circular 09/2026 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

note: The supply contract has statutory minimum contents and needs prior Ministry approval (Arts. 19(2), 20(1)); the worker signs a written placement contract in the model form (Art. 21).
source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 19–21 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

note: Orientation with a completion certificate is compulsory (Arts. 6(2)(c), 44(5), 65(2)) and covers rights and hotlines (Art. 65(1)); 74 periods under Circular 21/2021. The Law does not say who pays.
source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 6, 44, 65; Circular 21/2021 Art. 12 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

note: The Overseas Employment Support Fund (Arts. 66–68) supports early return, abuse, disputes and death; under Decision 34/2025/QĐ-TTg (replacing Decision 40/2021, from 15 September 2025) it pays half of lawyer and court costs up to VND 50 million, VND 40 million on death and half the cost of repatriating remains. Social insurance also applies.
source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 6, 66–68; Decision 34/2025/QĐ-TTg · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

note: The Ministry, with Foreign Affairs, posts officials to missions to manage workers abroad (Art. 70(2)(c)), and missions have statutory duties toward workers (Art. 71).
source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 70–71 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

note: Complaints go to the authority, which can sanction enterprises and order refunds with interest and compensation for damage caused (Decree 283/2026 Art. 49, replacing Decree 12/2022 from 10 September 2026); this is a remedial order, not an adjudicating body, and other claims go to the courts.
source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 6, 25, 69, 72; Decree 283/2026 Art. 49 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
note: Minimum age 18 (Art. 3(1)); prohibited jobs and areas (Art. 7(12)–(13)) are sex-neutral on their face.
source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 3, 7 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

note: The Ministry guides provinces, which may adopt support 'based on budget capacity'; employment service centers give labor-market information and enterprises help with job referral (Art. 60); psychosocial counseling is only encouraged (Art. 61). No public body has a duty to provide reintegration services. Recoded from 2 to 1 on 13 November 2026.
source: Law 69/2020 Arts. 60–61 · official text: https://vbpl.vn/

note: Overseas employment agencies need a licence from the Department of Labour, approved by the supervisory committee; the licence can be refused, suspended or revoked, and running an agency without a licence is punishable by up to 7 years' imprisonment. Agencies must take responsibility for contacting the employer abroad when a worker's rights are infringed, but the Law does not make them jointly liable with the employer.
source: Law Relating to Overseas Employment 1999, Chapters 4–6 · official text: https://www.mol.gov.mm/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/1999-OE-law.pdf

note: Service fees that the Department and agencies may charge are set under the Law (by the Central Committee, s. 6(g); s. 27 refers to fees set by the supervisory body); an agency that charges more than the fee set has its licence suspended or revoked and faces up to 3 years' imprisonment and a fine. The Law does not prohibit charging workers.
source: Ministry of Labour notifications; Law Relating to Overseas Employment 1999 · official text: https://www.mol.gov.mm/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/1999-OE-law.pdf

note: The 1999 Law does not require a written contract; it obliges the agency to carry out the obligations of a contract 'if there is one'. Contract signing between employer and worker before departure is handled administratively: an MOL announcement is titled on employer–worker contract signing and attendance at the overseas employment orientation course (mol.gov.mm post 37806; content not retrieved because the site blocked further access).
source: Law Relating to Overseas Employment 1999 · official text: https://www.mol.gov.mm/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/1999-OE-law.pdf

note: The 1999 Law only lets the supervisory body arrange training courses relating to overseas employment; it does not make orientation compulsory. MOL announcement titles refer to an overseas employment orientation course required in connection with contract signing and the Overseas Worker Identification Card (OWIC) (posts 37806, 35420, 34871; contents not retrieved).
source: Ministry of Labour · official text: https://www.mol.gov.mm/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/1999-OE-law.pdf

note: The 1999 Law creates no welfare fund and no compulsory insurance for overseas workers; it gives the worker a right to claim, through the agency, compensation for work injury abroad.
source: Law Relating to Overseas Employment 1999 · official text: https://www.mol.gov.mm/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/1999-OE-law.pdf

note: Labor attachés are posted in some destinations by administrative decision.
source: Ministry of Labour

note: The Department supervises agencies and the supervisory body can suspend or revoke licences; the worker may sue in civil or criminal courts for loss of rights relating to overseas employment. No specialized body awards compensation.
source: Law Relating to Overseas Employment 1999 · official text: https://www.mol.gov.mm/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/1999-OE-law.pdf

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
note: The Central Committee designates the countries, organizations and types of work for which overseas employment is not permitted, and the Department may stop a worker found unfit by the medical board from leaving; these powers are sex-neutral on their face.
source: Ministry of Labour announcements, 2014 and 2024 (to check) · official text: https://www.mol.gov.mm/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/1999-OE-law.pdf

note: The 1999 Law makes the systematic re-use at home of experience and skills gained abroad an objective and a duty of the Central Committee to guide and supervise, but it assigns no body a duty to provide reintegration services.
source: Ministry of Labour · official text: https://www.mol.gov.mm/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/1999-OE-law.pdf

note: Private recruitment agencies need an MLVT licence and a USD 100,000 deposit held in an MLVT account, are inspected and can be warned, suspended or have the licence withdrawn. Prakas 252/2013 makes the agency pay unpaid wages first when the embassy confirms them before repatriation, but no general joint liability with the foreign employer is written.
source: Sub-Decree No. 190 (2011); Prakas on recruitment agencies (2013) · official text: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/42-អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/178.html

note: Sub-Decree 190 sets no fee rule. Prakas 046/2013 leaves costs of finding work abroad to separate MLVT guidance for each destination; a 2026 MLVT notice fixes the service fee for farm work in Israel at about USD 3,800 and warns against overcharging. No general prohibition on charging workers was found.
source: Sub-Decree No. 190 (2011); Prakas (2013) · official text: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/កម្រងលិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្ត/3732.html

note: The agency must sign and carry out a contract with the Ministry, a recruitment service contract with the worker and an employment contract between the foreign employer and the worker. The employment contract must state working conditions, wages and benefits, be in Khmer, the destination language and English, and be sent to the Cambodian mission; contract models are set by Prakas and the contract must bear the signature of an MLVT representative. Prakas 253/2013 sets the minimum standard service
source: Sub-Decree No. 190 (2011); Prakas on contracts (2013) · official text: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/42-អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/178.html

note: Pre-departure orientation is compulsory and must follow the MLVT curriculum; it is delivered by the licensed agency in its training centre, and the Ministry issues a certificate that is required before the worker is sent. The texts do not say that orientation is free of charge to the worker.
source: Prakas on pre-departure orientation (2013) · official text: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/កម្រងលិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្ត/3732.html

note: There is no statutory welfare fund or compulsory insurance for migrant workers. The agency deposit (USD 100,000) held by the MLVT may be used to repatriate workers in force majeure, war, unrest or epidemics, or when an agency fails to settle disputes; agencies must help workers obtain the destination's social security and bear the repatriation of the body of a worker who dies abroad.
source: Sub-Decree No. 190 (2011) · official text: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/42-អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/178.html

note: Labour attachés or officers in charge of workers are posted at embassies and consulates in Thailand, Korea, Malaysia and Japan by government decision. Sub-Decree 190 does not require them, and the 2019–2023 Labour Migration Policy notes that they are not yet in all destination countries.

note: A complaints unit in the MLVT Department of Employment and Manpower and the provincial labour departments receives complaints from migrant workers, including money claims, and conciliates them; agreements are binding, and unresolved cases leave the parties to their legal rights. source: Prakas on the complaint mechanism (2013) · official text: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/កម្រងលិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្ត/3732.html

note: Recruiters must register as an enterprise and obtain an operating licence from the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare (MoLSW), and providing employment services without a licence is prohibited. Licences can be suspended or revoked. The agency answers for the interests of the workers it sends 'under the contract' and must compensate damage it causes, but no provision makes it jointly liable with the foreign employer.
source: Labour Law 2013; Decree on the Dispatch of Lao Workers to Work Abroad (2020) · official text: https://www.laoofficialgazette.gov.la/index.php?r=site/display&id=2154

note: The 2020 Decree leaves fees and service charges to a Presidential decree issued from time to time. The 2026 MoLSW Agreement caps the overseas placement fee at 3% of each month's salary under the contract. Collecting fees above set rates and taking deposits or collateral from workers are prohibited.
source: Decree on the Dispatch of Lao Workers to Work Abroad (2020) · official guidance: https://www.laoofficialgazette.gov.la/index.php?r=site/display&id=2550

note: Each worker must hold a commitment contract with the sending agency and a labour contract with the employer. The labour contract and the labour-supply contract are part of the licence file that MoLSW reviews before it licenses each sending. The Decree defines the labour contract as covering working conditions, wages, welfare and other terms, but sets no detailed minimum terms.
source: Labour Law 2013 · official text: https://www.laoofficialgazette.gov.la/index.php?r=site/display&id=1675

note: Training before departure is compulsory for the worker, and the sending agency must provide it. The province certifies the list of workers only after this training. No provision found says the training is free, or that it must cover rights and complaint channels.
source: Decree on the Dispatch of Lao Workers to Work Abroad (2020) · official text: https://www.laoofficialgazette.gov.la/index.php?r=site/display&id=1675

note: Workers and sending agencies must pay into a fund to assist Lao workers abroad, and workers must join social security under Lao law and the destination country's law. Agencies must lodge a guarantee deposit with MoLSW for helping workers in emergencies. No rules were found on the fund's benefits (death, disability, repatriation, legal aid).
source: Labour Law 2013 · official text: https://www.laoofficialgazette.gov.la/index.php?r=site/display&id=1675

note: MoLSW may propose appointing labour representatives to Lao diplomatic or consular missions 'where deemed necessary'. This is a discretionary power in a decree, not a statutory duty. Sending agencies must also keep their own representative abroad.
source: Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare · official text: https://www.laoofficialgazette.gov.la/index.php?r=site/display&id=1675

note: Workers may file complaints or petitions. MoLSW and the provincial and district labour offices must receive and resolve them, and can suspend or revoke licences. Violators may be ordered to pay civil damages, but no specialised body was found that awards compensation against recruiters or foreign employers. Labour disputes follow the Labour Law's mediation, administrative, committee and court routes.
source: Labour Law 2013 · official text: https://www.laoofficialgazette.gov.la/index.php?r=site/display&id=1675

note: The minimum age is 18. note: MoLSW and the provincial and district offices must 'encourage and promote' returnees to work at home and to upgrade their skills. This duty is in a decree, not a statute. note: No law or decree-law licensing private recruitment agencies for overseas work was found in the Jornal da República. The Labour Law applies only in the national territory.
